scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: Three tables
scenes.caption: At the discovery club, Tara finds a kitchen timer, a lamp and a prepared picture sorter. Each produces an output without another button press.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: A fixed countdown
scenes.caption: The timer follows instructions: count down from the chosen number, then ring. It does not need examples of earlier lunches. A device can be useful and automatic while following a fixed rule written by a person.
scenes.dialogue: Automatic does not settle the AI question.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: The lamp rule
scenes.caption: The lamp switches on when its light reading falls below a set threshold. Its instruction card states that rule. Tara now has evidence about this lamp, rather than a guess based on its shiny case or its sensor.
scenes.dialogue: A sensor alone does not show learning.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Open the model card
scenes.caption: The picture demonstration has labelled training examples and a separate test pack. Its predictions depend on patterns from examples. Choose what the club should inspect before describing another mystery device whose advertisement supplies no mechanism or test evidence at all.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: An honest label
scenes.caption: Tara requests a mechanism description. The mystery device stays marked unknown until evidence arrives. The prepared classifier is a classroom simulation, and a successful demonstration does not prove it will recognise every picture outside this carefully chosen collection of cards.
scenes.dialogue: Unknown is an evidence based answer.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: A new display
scenes.caption: Now a talking toy joins the display. A recorded greeting can sound clever without learning anything. In the lab, compare mechanisms, connect each claim to evidence and decide which questions would resolve uncertainty about this changed example.
